_about: ATTRIBUTE SCHEMA — a DATED SNAPSHOT, not a bare list.
verifiedAsOf / staleAfterDays: attribute templates move (Amazon retires keys and
renames others), so the schema carries the same verification discipline the rule
snapshot does. Staleness is ADVISORY (lib/audit/staleness.ts -> attributeSchemaStaleness)
source: WHO OWNS THE VALUE. "generated" = the model produces it from the listing’s
own facts. "operator" = a seller-account fact the app cannot know (price, SKU,
product id, model number, condition). Operator fields are filtered out of the
attributes prompt, deleted from generated output if the model volunteers one anyway,
and exempt from C23 completeness. A field with NO source reads as "generated" — the
stricter reading, because that is the one the gate can enforce.
enum: present ONLY where valueType is already "enum" AND the value set is genuinely
closed. The invariant valueType === "enum" <=> non-empty enum is asserted by
tests/attributeSchema.test.ts and by the pack-integrity manifest.
pendingTemplateConfirm: AM-7. The key sits outside the 24-key operational census we
have actually confirmed against a shipped listing, and the full Category Listing
Report is not yet available. The field is still produced and still checked; the flag
says the exact template key must be confirmed before an operator relies on it.

_declinedEnums._doc: ENUMS WE DECLINED TO ADD. An over-tight enum is not a stricter check — it is a gate that blocks a lawful value. Each of these fields LOOKS closed and is not.
_declinedEnums.item_form: Open in practice: capsule / tablet / softgel / gummy / powder / liquid / chewable / lozenge / effervescent tablet / stick pack / oil / cream / gel / serum — and new forms ship every year. Any list we wrote today would reject a lawful form tomorrow.
_declinedEnums.unit_count_type: Open in practice: Count / Ounce / Fluid Ounce / Gram / Millilitre / Pound / Servings and more, and the accepted token varies by category template. Enumerating it would fail listings whose template uses a synonym we did not list.
_declinedEnums.age_range_description: Open in practice: Adult / Kid / Teen / Baby / Toddler / Senior / All Ages, plus category-specific phrasings. It is also a FILTER FACET, so a rejected-but-lawful value costs discovery surface as well as a blocked run.

fields.label: Recommended Browse Nodes
fields.example: [NODE_ID] (suggestion only — confirm acceptance in Product Classifier)
fields.note: Suggestion only — confirm the node is accepted in the Product Classifier, and enter it LAST (after every other field is saved).

fields.label: Maximum Dosage
fields.example: 2 Capsules Daily (the maximum DOSE COUNT — never a strength/potency figure: gate C24 fails a dosage attribute that asserts one, because structured data states the number as a dose)

fields.label: Active Ingredients
fields.example: Actives only — must be a subset of ingredients and match the Supplement Facts panel

fields.label: Ingredients
fields.example: Full label list incl. Other Ingredients

fields.label: Allergen Information
fields.example: Contains: [ALLERGEN] — the exact canonical string, used whenever a declarable allergen is present

fields.label: Safety Warning
fields.example: Canonical safety text (allergen + pregnancy/nursing + physician consult + keep from children)

fields.label: Price
fields.note: Operator-owned. The app never invents a price: an invented price is a wrong price on a live listing.

fields.label: Subject Keyword (legacy platinum)
fields.example: Low weight today — fill only if template still exposes it
fields.note: Legacy platinum-keyword field. Weight today is negligible and it consumes NONE of the backend search-term byte budget, so filling it costs nothing and omitting it loses nothing — fill it only if the category template still exposes the key.

fields.label: External Product ID (GTIN/UPC/EAN)
fields.note: Operator-owned (GTIN/UPC/EAN or a GTIN exemption). Only the seller account knows it.

fields.label: Seller SKU
fields.note: Operator-owned. The seller’s own SKU, unknowable from a detail page.

fields.label: Model Number
fields.note: Operator-owned. Manufacturer model designation held in the seller’s records.

fields.label: Launch Date
fields.note: Operator-owned. WS2.1 named a launch date alongside price/GTIN/SKU and the schema had no field for it. It is an OFFER fact, not a product-copy fact: the date the seller wants the ASIN to become buyable is held in the seller account, the app cannot read it from a detail page, and a date this tool invented would be a wrong date on a live listing for exactly the reason an invented price is. Same treatment as the other four operator fields in consequence: withheld from the attributes prompt, deleted from generated output if the model volunteers one, and exempt from C23 completeness — so adding it can never fail a run that would otherwise pass.

fields.label: Condition
fields.note: Operator-owned. An offer fact, not a product-copy fact.
